fields.note: The shaft finish and speed rows are what separate a seal supplier from a rubber supplier. A rotary lip seal is a dynamic component: it runs against a moving surface, generates heat, and depends on a microscopic film of the medium to survive. Asking about the shaft, not just the seal, is the question a buyer remembers — and it is how a supplier avoids being blamed for a failure caused by a badly ground shaft

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: “Oil seal” is a shape, not a medium
The trade name covers every rotary shaft lip seal to DIN 3760, whatever it seals. In EPDM these run on water, coolant, steam and glycol — and not on mineral oil, which swells EPDM.
Shaft diameter, housing bore, width — and Type A or AS depending on whether you need a dust lip. Send those four and we can quote; a drawing is optional.
Tell us about the shaft, not just the seal
Surface finish, hardness and running speed decide how long a lip lasts. A badly ground shaft destroys a correct seal in weeks — so we ask about it before quoting, not afterwards.
The lip has to spring back
A shaft seal works because the lip recovers against its garter spring. We test compression set in-house to ASTM D395 Method B — a lip that takes a set stops sealing while it still looks perfect.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: The process depends on the assembly CONFIRM
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · “compression moulding” describes only part of a shaft seal

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The EPDM grade is set here for the medium — water, coolant, steam or glycol, never mineral oil.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The lip profile is the tool — its angle and contact width set the sealing force.
Moulding and metal bonding — the elastomer is moulded and bonded to the metal case in the same operation. Margo does rubber-to-metal bonding in-house (client-confirmed).
Lip trimming and spring fitting — the sealing edge is trimmed to profile and the garter spring fitted. Pending the assembly CONFIRM — if Margo supplies elements only, this step reads differently.
Quality inspection — lip concentricity, bore and width checked against DIN 3760, plus hardness and batch sampling.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Seals packed to protect the lip, which is damaged by stacking. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — but steps 03 and 04 describe a different operation from the live text. A rotary shaft seal is not simply a moulding: it is a bonded assembly with a fitted spring, and the live sequence describes only the rubber half.
Step 02 is worth the clause. The lip profile is where a shaft seal is won or lost, and naming it signals that Margo designs seals rather than copying them.
🛑 Steps 03 and 04 are the ones the CONFIRM rewrites — do not publish either until it is answered

notes: The process block must render from the part record. On this page it is wrong for a structural reason, not a wording one.
“Rubber-to-metal bonding” is a capability worth naming — it is client-confirmed and it is what makes a complete shaft seal possible.
